notes.note: The explanation of the jobs page behind its info button.

segment.source: Every change runs as a job with visible steps, a state and a way back. A job that needs a person, such as a manual step of a move, waits under Needs you until someone completes it.

notes.note: Subtitle of the audit log: the records read so far.

segment.source: {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}{more, select, yes { and more} other {}}

notes.note: The explanation of the audit log behind its info button.

segment.source: Each record carries the hash of the one before it, so the chain status above the list shows whether any record was changed or removed. The filters live in the address of the page, so a filtered view can be shared as a link.

notes.note: The explanation of the Discovery page behind its info button.

segment.source: The reconciler compares what the connectors, the probes, DHCP and DNS observe with what intent says, and proposes what a person should decide: devices it does not know, records without an owner, intent that differs from what is seen, and conflicts. Nothing changes until a person approves, and a rejection is remembered for its subject.

notes.note: Applied filter of the proposal inbox from a status bar link: the proposals to act on now (conflicts).
Applied filter of the proposal inbox from a status bar link: the proposals to review (every open one that is not a conflict).
The explanation of the reconciliation view behind its info button.

segment.source: Each row puts what intent, the DHCP leases, the DNS zones and the scans say about one address side by side. The rule of the row decides which of them wins; a conflict has no winner and waits for a person. The rows of one kind form one list, and the filters narrow every list to a network, a host or a kind.
